clue.text: Waterlogged ruins hastily emptied

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin, so 'ruins' is MARS

indicators.note: a word that is emptied loses all its inside letters, leaving only its two ends

parts.note: only the first and last letters of this word survive

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly bails out a flooded set of ancient ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that is soggy and boggy like a marsh is thoroughly soaked with water.

clue.text: Derided medium, shaken? Not right

indicators.note: 'not right' tells the solver to drop the letter standing for right from the word before

parts.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
shaken means jolted or rocked

explanation.surface: A psychic medium, rattled and mocked, is told they are wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic, but it is only the clothing-size letter; R is the usual abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to ridicule them with scorn, which is what deriding means.

clue.text: Disparage extremely tired summary

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to criticise or belittle, as a two-word verb
second meaning: exhausted and in poor health
third meaning: a brief ... of the main points

explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate senses of one phrase, read as verb, adjective and noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Belittling someone, feeling worn out, and a quick overview of events all share the same expression.

clue.text: Recast hero so he's symbol of good luck

indicators.note: to recast something is to mould it again into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A film role rewrites its hero so that he becomes a lucky mascot.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional lucky charm in British folk custom.

clue.text: Reform tailored for worshipper

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailor's alteration made to measure for a churchgoer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater pays religious devotion to idols or images, so is a kind of worshipper.

clue.text: Is success in exam ahead of one consumed by present objective?

indicators.note: what is consumed by something ends up inside it, so these letters go within the next word

parts.note: to present a gift is to donate it
taken as written
succeeding in an exam is a pass
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question about whether passing an exam beats being absorbed by one present goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like a noun meaning goal, but the definition is the adjective meaning impartial; the opening pieces all sit together inside the gift word.
explanation.definitionFit: An objective judgement is impartial and free of emotion, which is what dispassionate means.

clue.text: Behind schedule, keeping time for coffee

indicators.note: something keeping another thing holds it inside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: behind schedule means late
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone running late still makes time to grab a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso drink made with lots of steamed milk, a familiar type of coffee.

clue.text: Port having a sharper taste

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Moroccan seaport on the Strait of Gibraltar
second meaning: the comparative of an adjective for a zesty, sharp flavour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' could be the fortified wine, which fits the tasting surface, but here it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a North African harbour city, and a tangier food has a more pungent, zesty flavour.

clue.text: Traitor with energy after study covering information up

indicators.note: 'after' places the first-named piece behind the rest in the finished word
something covering another wraps around it, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A double agent swots up on stolen intelligence with great vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen, meaning the facts or the lowdown, is everyday British slang. Its reversal sits inside READ, and E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or party for its enemies, which makes them a traitor.

clue.text: Shrinks from agreements

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb for becoming smaller or tighter
second meaning: a noun for binding legal deals

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as someone backing away from deals; the two senses differ in stress and part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle that tightens gets smaller, and formal written deals between parties share the same spelling.

clue.text: Naturalist in wandering saw richer land

indicators.note: letters that are wandering drift out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A travelling naturalist roamed and found a more fertile country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian scientist who sailed on the Beagle and proposed evolution by natural selection was a famous naturalist.

clue.text: Number ahead in projection

indicators.note: 'ahead' puts the first piece at the front of the word that follows it

parts.note: a number
in and on both mean present or at home, taking part

explanation.surface: A figure leading the way in some plan or forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projection' looks like a forecast, but here it is a jutting piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry, a tenon is the tongue projecting from one timber that fits into a mortise in another.

clue.text: Destroy poem after hesitation

indicators.note: 'after' puts the first-named piece behind the following one

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A poet hesitates and then tears up their verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind and water wear away and gradually ruin rock, so eroding is a slow kind of destroying.

clue.text: Article by joker filled with knowledge, popular and inspiring

indicators.note: something filled with other things holds them inside it

parts.note: the indefinite article
a wag is a witty joker
ken means range of knowledge
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by a clever, well-liked comic proves uplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken, as in 'beyond my ken', is an old Scots word for knowledge; both it and the popular word go inside the joker together.
explanation.definitionFit: An awakening experience rouses fresh understanding or feeling, which is close to stirring or inspiring.

clue.text: Odd loner, brash, playing without rules

indicators.note: letters that are playing around are moving about freely, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An eccentric, brash recluse ignores every rule of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from wrestling, where every grip is permitted, so it means with no restrictions.

clue.text: Land, not hot, inhabited by northern people in alliance

indicators.note: a place inhabited by people has them living inside it
'not hot' tells the solver to drop the letter standing for hot

parts.note: a bird or plane lands, or alights
N is the abbreviation for northern
men are people

explanation.surface: A cool country settled by tribes from the north that have joined forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' reads as a country but is the verb, as a bird lands; H is the tap abbreviation for hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Nations in alignment are lined up together on the same side, as in a political alliance.

clue.text: Fish cut up? Not easy

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to clip is to cut
hard is the opposite of easy

explanation.surface: Someone finds gutting and slicing a fish rather difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like filleting, but 'up' is a separate instruction for the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Artist, demon with racket, endlessly going back into combat

parts.note: an imp is a small demon

indicators.note: a word going into another sits inside it

parts.note: to combat something is to resist it

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read backwards
something endlessly given loses its final letter

parts.note: a racket is a din, or noise

explanation.surface: A painter fights a little devil wielding a tennis racket in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests tennis, but it is a din; the shortened, turned-round din sits inside the combat word after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Monet and Renoir were Impressionists, members of a French school of painters, so one is an artist.

clue.text: Incentive, first off, to join outfit for activity

indicators.note: 'first off' means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a spur is an incentive
a suit is an outfit

explanation.surface: A sales incentive to buy new kit for an outdoor sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit is a hobby or pastime that someone spends time on, meaning an activity.

clue.text: Silly to plead for larva

indicators.note: silly means foolish or nonsensical, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: It is foolish to beg on behalf of a grub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the aquatic larval stage of a frog or toad before it grows legs.

clue.text: Comrade, loud and clear, capturing hearts of fiery romantics

indicators.note: something capturing another takes it inside

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
to clear a place of something is to rid it

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so the middle letter of each is kept

parts.note: the centre letter of this five-letter word
the centre letter of this nine-letter word

explanation.surface: A comrade speaks out loudly and plainly, winning over passionate dreamers.
explanation.definitionFit: A comrade is a companion or ally, someone close, so a friend in everyday terms.

clue.text: Element first of all used by artist making pasta sauce

parts.note: carbon is a chemical element

indicators.note: 'first of' keeps only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its opening letter
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A chemist's ingredient is used first by a painter cooking up a sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of all' reads as 'firstly', but it picks the first letter of 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonara is an Italian sauce for spaghetti made with egg, cheese and cured pork.

clue.text: External course, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter moves to the end, rotating the word by one place

parts.note: a route is a course taken

explanation.surface: An outside track at a racecourse, with the front runner ending last.
explanation.definitionFit: Something external lies on the outside, which is exactly what outer describes.

clue.text: Low point in production, a dirge

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: A mournful lament marks the low point of a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, literally the point of the sky directly below an observer.

clue.text: Depth in error, not fine for mature person

indicators.note: a piece placed in another word sits within it
'not fine' tells the solver to drop the letter standing for fine

parts.note: a fault is an error
D is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A grown-up's profound mistake, judged not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: F for fine, as on pencil leads, drops from FAULT, and D goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fully grown, mature person is an adult, as opposed to a child.

clue.text: Sad and single, after love in network, for example

indicators.note: 'after' places the first-named piece behind those that follow
a letter placed in a word goes inside it

parts.note: a web is a network
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
e.g. abbreviates for example
single means one

explanation.surface: A lonely single person, unlucky in love on a dating network, feels down.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone describes a person looking sorrowful and miserable, a strong word for sad.

clue.text: Overthrow ended with detention of the confused king

indicators.note: detention means holding someone in, so these letters are held inside

parts.note: done means finished, ended

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A coup ends with the bewildered monarch locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for Rex, Latin for king; 'detention' signals holding letters inside the word for ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To dethrone a monarch is to remove them from power, which is to overthrow them.

clue.text: Thanks returned by nurse? Listen

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
to nurse someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Thanking a nurse who asks, 'Are you listening?'
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to someone is to pay close heed to what they say, an older sense of listening.
